reference_prolog:
% Self-contained SWI-Prolog program
% Jurisdiction: North Carolina
% Focus year: 2021
% Question: Is an officer of the court an individual empowered by law to execute a writ of eviction?

% ----------------------------
% Basic domain modeling
% ----------------------------

state(north_carolina).
focus_year(2021).

% We treat "writ of eviction" as a "writ for possession of real property" (summary ejectment context).
writ_type(writ_of_eviction).
writ_type(writ_for_possession_of_real_property).

writ_synonym(writ_of_eviction, writ_for_possession_of_real_property).
writ_synonym(writ_for_possession_of_real_property, writ_for_possession_of_real_property).

% ----------------------------
% Statute translation (NCGS  42-36.2 (2021))
% ----------------------------

% NCGS  42-36.2(a) (2021): "Before removing ... pursuant to a writ ... the sheriff shall give the tenant notice ..."
% Also: "The time within which the sheriff shall have to execute the writ shall be no more than five days
% from the sheriff's receipt thereof."
statute_42_36_2_applies_to_executor_role(north_carolina, 2021, sheriff).

statute_42_36_2_execution_deadline_days(north_carolina, 2021, 5).

% Encodes that (for covered writs) the statute assigns execution/removal actions to the sheriff.
% This is used as the legal source for "empowered by law to execute" in this narrow statute-based model.
statute_42_36_2_executor_empowered_by_law(State, Year, WritType, Role) :-
    statute_42_36_2_applies_to_executor_role(State, Year, Role),
    writ_synonym(WritType, writ_for_possession_of_real_property).

% Optional: encode that the sheriff has a duty to give notice before removing property (not needed to answer,
% but included as a faithful statutory duty/threshold translation).
statute_42_36_2_requires_notice_before_removal(State, Year, Role) :-
    statute_42_36_2_applies_to_executor_role(State, Year, Role).

% ----------------------------
% Scenario facts (the question's factual statement)
% ----------------------------

% The individual we are evaluating.
person(officer_court_1).

% "Officer of the court" status (as stated in the question).
person_role(officer_court_1, officer_of_the_court).

% The question is about executing a writ of eviction.
scenario_writ(writ_of_eviction).

% Helper predicate that succeeds when the scenario (as encoded) holds.
scenario_statement :-
    state(north_carolina),
    focus_year(2021),
    person(officer_court_1),
    person_role(officer_court_1, officer_of_the_court),
    scenario_writ(writ_of_eviction).

% ----------------------------
% Legal reasoning helpers
% ----------------------------

% A person is "empowered by law to execute" a writ (in this dataset) if the statute identifies their role
% as the executor for the writ-for-possession / eviction context.
empowered_by_law_to_execute_writ(Person, WritType) :-
    scenario_statement,
    focus_year(Year),
    state(State),
    person_role(Person, Role),
    statute_42_36_2_executor_empowered_by_law(State, Year, WritType, Role).

% ----------------------------
% Answer predicate (must be deterministic yes/no)
% ----------------------------

housing_answer(yes) :-
    scenario_writ(WritType),
    empowered_by_law_to_execute_writ(officer_court_1, WritType),
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    !.

% ----------------------------
% Main entrypoint + initialization (REQUIRED)
% ----------------------------

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: Is an officer of the court an individual empowered by law to execute a writ of eviction?
